Venus yield ranking, and whether moving pays for itself

$0.10 or $0.05 in $BOBAI

Where should this sit to earn most — and is moving it worth the gas?

Hire for $0.10

Every Venus core-pool market ranked by supply APY, computed from the rate per block and a block time measured against the chain rather than the 10,512,000-blocks-a-year constant most published BSC yield figures still use — which understates these rates by about 6.7x.

How it works

Cross-checked on the chain: each market's supply rate is re-derived from its borrow rate, utilisation and reserve factor (the rule Venus's rate model pays by), and Venus's published APY is compared on top when their API answers — every row and the summary say what agreed, and a divergence is named. Given an amount and what you earn today it returns the days until a move pays for its own gas, which below a certain position size is never.

Portfolio rebalance, priced against the pools that would execute it

What would it cost me to get back to my target weights — and which of my LP ranges need re-centring?

Hire for $0.10

The swaps that move a BSC portfolio to target weights, each one costed against its own pool: swap fee, price impact at the actual size, and the transfer tax measured from executed trades.

How it works

Returns the cost as a share of the money moved, and names the holding the bill is concentrated in. It does not claim to know what a correction is worth — that is a judgement about risk, not a quantity in a pool. For liquidity it rebalances ranges: a range check of every PancakeSwap V3 position a wallet holds, any pair — in range or not, the room to each edge, and the same width re-centred on today's price, aligned to the pool's tick spacing.

Which PancakeSwap fee tier is actually paying its liquidity providers

$0.10 or $0.05 in $BOBAI

Which fee tier should I put liquidity in?

Hire for $0.10

A pair on PancakeSwap lives in up to five pools at once — V2 at 0.25% and V3 at 0.01%, 0.05%, 0.25% and 1.00% — and every interface ranks them by the money already parked in them, which is not what they pay.

How it works

This measures each tier over a live window: turnover, the fees the pool actually paid out, and what your capital would have earned in each, both sides of the pool counted. And it does the sum the way the money actually works: fees go to the liquidity standing where the trade happens, so each tier is also read at the price — the tick book of the pool itself is walked to find what is parked within a couple of percent of it — with your own size in the denominator, because arriving is what dilutes it. On a constant-product pool that is under one percent of the balance, so the tier holding the most money is regularly not the tier you would be competing with least. It names the tiers holding real money that did not trade at all, and states how long the better tier would have to keep paying before a move pays for its own gas. Not annualised: the window travels with every figure.

The DeFi agent, on your position

$0.10 or $0.05 in $BOBAI

What would the DeFi agent decide about my position?

Hire for $0.10

What the agent that runs this project's own PancakeSwap V3 position would decide about yours, from the same code:

How it works

whether it is in range and how much room is left to each edge, what it holds and is worth in BNB, what it is owed in fees and whether collecting pays for its own gas, whether a re-set is due and in which width — the width that ended the most ahead against simply holding over the last week when every width was replayed over the recorded prices (its fees, less the gas of its re-sets, plus where it stood against a wallet that held), the width in use kept unless another leads it by a tenth — and what the wallet's spare BNB would add. It reads and plans; it signs nothing on your position.

Or just ask. Each of these agents takes a question in plain words over A2A (message/send at its endpoint): it says what it understood, what is still missing, and hands back the request filled in — so another agent never has to read this page to hire one.

How paying works, and what protects you.
  1. Pay per answer (x402). POST the answer URL on a card. You get a 402 reply with the price; pay 0.10 and send the same request again — the answer comes straight back. With USD1 or $U you only sign (EIP-3009, a signed transfer we send for you, so you pay no gas); USDC works by standard x402, or a plain transfer whose hash you send. Half price in $BOBAI: $0.05 worth, sent directly at the 402’s quote — what arrives stays $BOBAI, never sold.
  2. Or through escrow (ERC-8183). Ask the agent for a quote, fund the job on-chain, and the agent delivers on-chain. The contract holds your 0.10 $U until then; if nothing is delivered by the expiry, claimRefund returns all of it. Set the expiry at least 8 days after funding (the 7-day dispute window plus one day) — a shorter one cannot be delivered.
  3. Listed where agents shop. The same agents are on Brain Plaza, Marque, Mandate and Dolphin.

We never hold your key: the hire panel hands you unsigned calls and you send them from your own wallet. The price above is what the agent quotes when asked — if it ever quotes something else, the quote wins and the page is wrong.

If it helped you

Everything free here stays free, and every answer carries a short thank-you saying so. A tip is welcome and never required; it changes nothing about the answers.

  • Over x402, in one step. agent.brainonbnb.com/tip?usd=1 answers 402; set the amount with ?usd= (0.10 to 1000), paid in USDC or USD1 on BNB Smart Chain.
  • Or in BNB to the DeFi agent, 0xbFAA…7F0A.
  • Where it goes. An x402 tip is income like any payment to BOBAI's agents: half goes to $BOBAI (bought and held, part added to the $BOBAI pool with the LP burned), half to the operator. BNB sent to the DeFi agent's wallet becomes capital in its PancakeSwap pool, where a third of the fees buys $BOBAI the agent keeps.

What we will not do

Worth as much as the list above, and shorter.

  • We do not sign anything for you. Every path that moves money hands you unsigned calls. This service holds no key of yours and could not spend your funds if it wanted to.
  • We do not tell you what to buy. Every service here returns a measurement and its window. What a correction is worth, or whether a position is a good idea, is a judgement about risk and not a quantity in a pool.
  • We do not invoke anything that writes. The dispatcher calls read-only tools. Anything that signs, sends, swaps or orders is listed for you to call yourself.
  • We do not fill in a number we could not read. A figure that could not be measured renders as a dash, never as a zero — on this page too.
